ideal: It must be possible for a quantifier whose variable has a further condition to also be a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing.
note: one sentence, no numbered name

ideal: When a definition with an or inside one kind can be said kind by kind, the verbalizer says it as one run of clauses joined by commas and "or".
note: condition up front, "it" for the definition

ideal: It must be possible that a document starts with a refused frontmatter, the checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read, and some run exits with code 2.
note: one sentence; the run stays unlinked to the document, as in the formula

ideal:
When a document keeps no readings, no word declared by a unit it holds is reported by the checker, and none is:
- a word that a reading says and nothing declares
- a word declared in a unit that is not a term
- a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration
- a word that no claim, definition or fact uses
note: "none is" list replaces five "is not" lines

ideal: The checker reports a finding for every unit that is unfounded, miscited or circular.
note: three parallel rules merged into one with "or"

ideal: It must be possible that a bug names an issue the tracker knows and has not closed, an expected failure checks that bug, and the checker reports no finding for the bug or for the expected failure.
note: one sentence chaining bug, issue and expected failure

ideal: A word that some unit declares but that no claim, definition or fact of any unit uses is a word that no claim, definition or fact uses.
note: both conditions folded into the subject

ideal: The checker never reports the formula of a unit as lone on a word that is not a signature.
note: condition becomes a relative clause on the word

ideal: Every unclosed frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: "every" instead of a quantifier header

ideal: When the project has a runner, the checker reports an untesting for every unguarded claim.
note: the project condition moved out of the quantifier

ideal: It must be possible that the verbalizer fails on the formula of some unit with a fault of its own.
note: "some unit" inline

ideal: When a list is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, and its second side begins with a time phrase but its first side does not, the verbalizer says it with "then" before the time phrase.
note: the two time-phrase conditions joined with "but"

ideal: When a document is another document without its frontmatter, the two hold exactly the same units, and the checker reports a finding for one exactly when it reports a finding for the other.
note: two-way implications said as "exactly the same" and "exactly when"

ideal: When the project has no tracker, the checker reports no untracking for any unit.
note: condition up front, "any unit"

ideal: The checker names every unit that is held with units that cannot all hold in its report of a contradiction, and for every scenario that cannot happen while every held unit holds, it reports that the scenario cannot happen.
note: list of two rules made one sentence

ideal: When a frontmatter lists a missing plugin, the checker reports that the project lacks that plugin.
note: "a ... that" instead of "every ... the"

ideal: When a document starts with no listing frontmatter and the command line of a run does not name it, the checker runs no plugin over it.
note: "runs no plugin" replaces the quantifier over plugins

ideal: When a list is a rule whose first side begins with a time phrase, the verbalizer says it with "then" on a line of its own at the start of the second side.
note: "it" for the list

ideal: The verbalizer says in full, with "there is" and the numbered name, every quantifier with several conditions one of which begins with a time phrase.
note: condition becomes the object's description

ideal: When a document keeps readings, the checker reports the statement of every unit it holds that holds a formula and whose statement is not current.
note: four conditions folded into one noun phrase

ideal: Every misquoted frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: "every" instead of a quantifier header

ideal: It must be possible that a unit holds a formula, a claim, a definition or a fact of the unit uses a signature, and the checker does not report the formula of the unit as lone on that signature.
note: one sentence, no numbered names

ideal: A run that asks for a logic command exits with code 0 when the checker reports no scenario as one that cannot happen and no unit is held with units that cannot all hold.
note: the run's request becomes its description

ideal: When a unit holds a formula that can be said in words but has no statement, the statement of the unit is unwritten.
note: three conditions in one clause

ideal: When a run asks for a command that is not available, the checker reports it as an unknown command and the run exits with code 2.
note: "a command that is not available" replaces the numbered name

ideal: Every unterminated frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: "every" instead of a quantifier header

ideal: When a quantifier fits a noun phrase and its variable is the subject of the sentence, the verbalizer says it with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1".
note: makes clear it is the quantifier that fits a noun phrase

ideal: When a run asks for a generate command, the checker says why the formula of each unit that cannot be said in words cannot be said, and if there is such a unit, the run does not exit with code 0.
note: split what holds per unit from what holds for the run

ideal: It must be possible for a definition with an or inside one kind to have an alternative that does not begin with its kind.
note: second membership said as a property of the first

ideal:
At every moment, when a failing cleanup runs on an owner that pulse has disposed:
- from then on, the dispose of the owner never throws
- then or later, the error of the cleanup reaches the nearest error handler or boundary above the owner, if the owner has one
note: two rules share one trigger; owner_3 becomes "the nearest ... if the owner has one"

ideal: When a document is another document without its frontmatter, the checker reports a finding for one exactly when it reports a finding for the other.
note: two implications said as "exactly when"

ideal: Every foreign frontmatter is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
note: "every" instead of a quantifier header

ideal: When a document starts with a refused frontmatter, the checker reports that the document has a frontmatter it cannot read.
note: "a" instead of "every ... the"

ideal: The verbalizer says in full, with "there is" and the numbered name, every quantifier whose condition is not about its variable.
note: condition becomes the object's description

ideal: A run that gets code 2 from any plugin exits with code 2, and a run that gets code 1 from some plugin and code 2 from none exits with code 1.
note: list of two rules made one sentence

ideal: The checker reports a finding for every hidden conflict.
note: "hidden conflict" for "conflict that is hidden"

ideal: The checker does not report that a scenario cannot happen when it can happen while every held unit holds.
note: "it" for the scenario, no numbered name

ideal: The verbalizer says every list that can be put in a sentence in a sentence.
note: condition becomes the object's description

ideal: The checker never reports the formula of a term as lone on any word.
note: "never ... any" replaces the double quantifier
